Configuration options\n   */\n  constructor(options = {}) {\n    this.options = {\n      minDataPoints: parseInt(process.env.BEHAVIOR_MIN_DATA_POINTS || '10'),\n      insightRefreshInterval: parseInt(process.env.BEHAVIOR_INSIGHT_REFRESH_INTERVAL || '86400000'), // 24 hours\n      segmentationThreshold: parseInt(process.env.BEHAVIOR_SEGMENTATION_THRESHOLD || '50'),\n      ...options\n    };\n\n    // Storage for insights and user data\n    this.userInsights = new Map();\n    this.userSegments = new Map();\n    this.dataSources = new Map();\n    this.insightGenerationTimes = new Map();\n\n    logger.info('User Behavior Insights Service initialized with options:', {\n      minDataPoints: this.options.minDataPoints,\n      insightRefreshInterval: this.options.insightRefreshInterval,\n      segmentationThreshold: this.options.segmentationThreshold\n    });\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Register a data source for user behavior analysis\n   * @param {Object} dataSource - Data source configuration\n   * @returns {Object} - Registration result\n   */\n  registerDataSource(dataSource) {\n    try {\n      const { id, name, description, type, fetchFunction } = dataSource;\n\n      if (!id) {\n        throw new Error('Data source ID is required');\n      }\n\n      if (!name) {\n        throw new Error('Data source name is required');\n      }\n\n      if (!type) {\n        throw new Error('Data source type is required');\n      }\n\n      if (!fetchFunction || typeof fetchFunction !== 'function') {\n        throw new Error('Data source must provide a fetchFunction');\n      }\n\n      // Store data source\n      this.dataSources.set(id, {\n        id,\n        name,\n        description: description || '',\n        type,\n        fetchFunction,\n        registeredAt: new Date().toISOString()\n      });\n\n      logger.info(`Registered user behavior data source: ${name}`, { id, type });\n      return { success: true, id, name };\n    } catch (error) {\n      logger.error('Error registering data source:', error.message);\n      return { success: false, error: error.message };\n    }\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Generate insights for a specific user\n   * @param {string} userId - Integration disabled.');\n      this.options.enabled = false;\n      return;\n    }\n\n    // Start timer for batch sending\n    this.sendTimer = setInterval(() => {\n      this._processBatch();\n    }, this.options.sendInterval);\n\n    logger.info('Analytics integration initialized with endpoint:', this.options.endpoint);\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Track a conversation event\n   * @param {Object} event -             "full_content": "# Analytics Service\n\n## Overview\n\nThe Analytics Service is a core component of the chatbot platform that tracks, processes, and analyzes conversation data to provide insights and metrics about chatbot performance and user interactions.\n\n## Features\n\n- **Message Tracking**: Tracks user and bot messages with detailed metrics\n- **Analytics Aggregation**: Aggregates metrics by period (daily, weekly, monthly, all-time)\n- **Report Generation**: Generates comprehensive reports with metrics, trends, and insights\n- **Performance Monitoring**: Tracks response times and other performance metrics\n- **Sentiment Analysis**: Analyzes sentiment in user messages\n- **Top Entities/Intents/Queries**: Identifies most common entities, intents, and user queries\n\n## Installation\n\nThe Analytics Service is part of the chatbot platform and does not require separate installation. Simply ensure that the MongoDB connection is properly configured in your environment.\n\n## Usage\n\n### Basic Usage\n\n```javascript\nconst AnalyticsService = require('./analytics.service');\n\n// Initialize the service\nconst analyticsService = new AnalyticsService();\n\n// Track a user message\nawait analyticsService.trackMessage({\n  chatbotId: 'chatbot123',\n  type: 'user',\n  text: 'Hello, how can you help me today?',\n  userId: 'user123',\n  timestamp: new Date(),\n  intent: 'greeting',\n  entities: [{ type: 'greeting', value: 'hello' }],\n  sentiment: 'positive'\n});\n\n// Get analytics for a specific period and date\nconst dailyAnalytics = await analyticsService.getAnalytics('chatbot123', 'daily', new Date());\n\n// Get all-time analytics\nconst allTimeAnalytics = await analyticsService.getAllTimeAnalytics('chatbot123');\n\n// Generate a report for a specific period and date range\nconst report = await analyticsService.generateReport(\n  'chatbot123',\n  'weekly',\n  new Date(Date.now() - 7 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000), // 7 days ago\n  new Date() // today\n);\n```\n\n### Advanced Usage\n\nFor more advanced usage, see the [Analytics Service Documentation](../../docs/analytics-service.md).\n\n## API Reference\n\n### `trackMessage(message)`\n\nTracks a message (user or bot) and updates analytics in the database.\n\n**Parameters:**\n\n- `message` (Object): The message to track\n  - `chatbotId` (String): ID of the chatbot\n  - `type` (String): Type of message ('user' or 'bot')\n  - `text` (String): Message text\n  - `userId` (String): ID of the user\n  - `timestamp` (Date): Message timestamp\n  - `intent` (String, optional): Intent of the message\n  - `entities` (Array, optional): Entities in the message\n  - `sentiment` (String, optional): Sentiment of the message\n\n**Returns:**\n\n- Promise that resolves when the message is tracked\n\n### `getAnalytics(chatbotId, period, date)`\n\nRetrieves analytics for a specific period and date.\n\n**Parameters:**\n\n- `chatbotId` (String): ID of the chatbot\n- `period` (String): Period to retrieve ('daily', 'weekly', 'monthly')\n- `date` (Date): Date to retrieve analytics for\n\n**Returns:**\n\n- Promise that resolves to the analytics document or null if not found\n\n### `getAllTimeAnalytics(chatbotId)`\n\nRetrieves all-time analytics for a chatbot.\n\n**Parameters:**\n\n- `chatbotId` (String): ID of the chatbot\n\n**Returns:**\n\n- Promise that resolves to the all-time analytics document or null if not found\n\n### `generateReport(chatbotId, period, startDate, endDate)`\n\nGenerates a comprehensive report with metrics, trends, and insights.\n\n**Parameters:**\n\n- `chatbotId` (String): ID of the chatbot\n- `period` (String): Period to generate report for ('daily', 'weekly', 'monthly')\n- `startDate` (Date): Start date of the report\n- `endDate` (Date): End date of the report\n\n**Returns:**\n\n- Promise that resolves to a report object with metrics, trends, and insights\n\n## Testing\n\nThe Analytics Service is tested using Jest. To run the tests:\n\n```bash\nnpx jest src/tests/unit/services/analytics.service.test.js\n```\n\n## Demo\n\nA demo script is available to showcase the Analytics Service capabilities:\n\n```bash\nnode src/tests/scripts/analytics-demo.js\n```\n\n## Contributing\n\nTo contribute to the Analytics Service:\n\n1. Express request object\n * @param {Object} res - Express response object\n * @param {Function} next - Express next function\n */\nexports.authenticateToken = async (req, res, next) => {\n  try {\n    // Check for Authorization header\n    const authHeader = req.headers.authorization;\n    \n    if (!authHeader) {\n      req.user = null;\n      return res.status(401).json({ error: 'Authentication required' });\n    }\n\n    // Check for proper Bearer format\n    if (!authHeader.startsWith('Bearer ')) {\n      req.user = null;\n      return res.status(401).json({ error: 'Invalid authorization format' });\n    }\n\n    // Extract token\n    const token = authHeader.substring(7); // Remove 'Bearer ' prefix\n    \n    if (!token) {\n      req.user = null;\n      return res.status(401).json({ error: 'Authentication required' });\n    }\n\n    try {\n      // Verify token\n      const decoded = await authService.verifyToken(token);\n      \n      if (!decoded || !decoded.userId) {\n        req.user = null;\n        return res.status(401).json({ error: 'Invalid token' });\n      }\n\n      // Get user by ID using the userId from the decoded token\n      const user = await authService.getUserById(decoded.userId);\n      \n      // Check if user exists\n      if (!user) {\n        req.user = null;\n        return res.status(401).json({ error: 'User not found' });\n      }\n\n      // Attach user to request\n      req.user = user;\n      next();\n    } catch (error) {\n      logger.error('Token verification error:', error);\n      req.user = null;\n      return res.status(401).json({ error: 'Invalid token' });\n    }\n  } catch (error) {\n    logger.error('Auth middleware error:', error);\n    req.user = null;\n    return res.status(401).json({ error: 'Invalid token' });\n  }\n};\n\n/**\n * Check if user has required role\n * @param {string|Array} roles - Entity object\n   * @param {string} text - Text to analyze\n   * @returns {Array} Matching values\n   * @private\n   */\n  extractEntityMatches(entity, text) {\n    const matches = [];\n    const lowerText = text.toLowerCase();\n    \n    // Check each value for matches\n    for (const value of entity.values) {\n      const synonyms = [value.value, ...(value.synonyms || [])];\n      \n      for (const synonym of synonyms) {\n        const lowerSynonym = synonym.toLowerCase();\n        \n        if (lowerText.includes(lowerSynonym)) {\n          matches.push({\n            value: value.value,\n            synonym: synonym,\n            index: lowerText.indexOf(lowerSynonym),\n            length: lowerSynonym.length\n          });\n        }\n      }\n    }\n    \n    return matches;\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Invalidate entity cache entries\n   * @param {string} entityId - It centralizes database operations, implements query optimization, adds caching capabilities, provides consistent error handling, and supports transaction management.\n\n## Architecture\n\nThe data layer consists of the following components:\n\n- **BaseRepository**: Abstract base class providing common CRUD operations and query optimization capabilities\n- **Model-specific Repositories**: Extend BaseRepository to provide model-specific optimized queries and caching\n- **DatabaseService**: Manages MongoDB connection and provides access to repositories\n\n## Features\n\n- **Centralized Data Access**: All database operations are performed through repositories\n- **Query Optimization**: Optimized queries with proper indexing and projection\n- **Caching**: In-memory caching with TTL for frequently accessed data\n- **Error Handling**: Consistent error handling and logging\n- **Transaction Support**: Methods for transaction management\n- **Connection Management**: Centralized connection handling with event listeners\n\n## Usage\n\n### Connecting to the Database\n\n```javascript\nconst { databaseService } = require('../data');\n\n// Connect to the database\nawait databaseService.connect();\n\n// Disconnect when done\nawait databaseService.disconnect();\n```\n\n### Using Repositories\n\n```javascript\nconst { repositories } = require('../data');\n\n// Get a                 "full_content": "/**\n * Adaptive TTL Strategy\n * \n * Dynamically adjusts cache TTL based on usage patterns\n * - Frequently accessed resources get longer TTL\n * - Resources with high miss rates get shorter TTL\n * - Resources with high latency get longer TTL\n */\n\nconst { redisClient } = require('./redis.client');\nconst logger = require('@src/utils/logger');\nconst cacheMonitoring = require('@services/monitoring/cache-efficiency');\n\n// Default TTL values in seconds\nconst DEFAULT_TTL = 3600; Access Frequency Factor (higher frequency = longer TTL)\n    // Normalize access count against the highest access count in this resource type\n    const maxAccess = Object.values(accessTracking[resourceType] || {})\n      .reduce((max, access) => Math.max(max, access.count), 1);\n    const accessFrequencyFactor = resourceAccess.count / maxAccess;\n    \n    // 2. Message text\n   * @param {String} userId - User ID\n   * @param {String} chatbotId - Chatbot ID\n   * @param {String} conversationId - Conversation ID\n   * @returns {Promise<Array>} - Detected topics\n   */\n  async detectTopics(message, userId, chatbotId, conversationId) {\n    try {\n      // Use local NLP models to detect topics\n      // This is a simplified implementation - in a real system, you would use\n      // more sophisticated NLP techniques like topic modeling (LDA, NMF)\n      const topics = await this._extractTopicsFromText(message);\n      \n      // Track detected topics\n      const trackedTopics = [];\n      for (const topicData of topics) {\n        const topic = await this.trackTopic(topicData, userId, chatbotId, conversationId);\n        trackedTopics.push(topic);\n      }\n      \n      return trackedTopics;\n    } catch (error) {\n      logger.error('Error detecting topics:', error);\n      throw error;\n    }\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Extract topics from text using NLP techniques\n   * @param {String} text - Input text\n   * @returns {Promise<Array>} - Extracted topics\n   * @private\n   */\n  async _extractTopicsFromText(text) {\n    try {\n      // In a real implementation, this would use a local NLP model\n      // For this example, we'll use a simplified approach\n      \n      // Common topics with keywords\n      const topicKeywords = {\n        'technology': ['computer', 'software', 'hardware', 'tech', 'digital', 'ai', 'artificial intelligence', 'machine learning'],\n        'travel': ['trip', 'vacation', 'hotel', 'flight', 'destination', 'tourism', 'travel'],\n        'food': ['restaurant', 'recipe', 'cooking', 'meal', 'dish', 'food', 'cuisine'],\n        'health': ['fitness', 'exercise', 'diet', 'health', 'wellness', 'medical'],\n        'business': ['company', 'startup', 'entrepreneur', 'market', 'business', 'finance', 'investment'],\n        'education': ['school', 'university', 'learning', 'student', 'teacher', 'course', 'education']\n      };\n      \n      const detectedTopics = [];\n      const lowerText = text.toLowerCase();\n      \n      // Check for each topic's keywords in the text\n      for (const [topic, keywords] of Object.entries(topicKeywords)) {\n        let score = 0;\n        let matchedKeywords = [];\n        \n        for (const keyword of keywords) {\n          if (lowerText.includes(keyword)) {\n            score += 1;\n            matchedKeywords.push(keyword);\n          }\n        }\n        \n        // If we found keywords for this topic, add it to detected topics\n        if (score > 0) {\n          detectedTopics.push({\n            name: topic,\n            confidence: Math.min(score / 3, 1), // Normalize confidence\n            keywords: matchedKeywords,\n            metadata: {\n              keywordCount: matchedKeywords.length\n            }\n          });\n        }\n      }\n      \n      // Sort by confidence\n      return detectedTopics.sort((a, b) => b.confidence - latestReference.timestamp) / (1000 * 60 * 60) : 0; // Hours ago\n        \n        // Calculate frequency\n        const frequencyScore = topicReferences.length;\n        \n        // Combined relevance score (higher is more relevant)\n        const relevanceScore = (frequencyScore * 0.7) + ((24 - Math.min(recencyScore, 24)) / 24 * 0.3);\n        \n        return {\n          ...topic.toObject(),\n          relevanceScore,\n          references: topicReferences.length\n        };\n      });\n      \n      // Sort by relevance\n      return topicsWithRelevance.sort((a, b) => b.relevanceScore - a.relevanceScore);\n    } catch (error) {\n      logger.error('Error getting conversation topics:', error);\n      throw error;\n    }\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Get user's topic history\n   * @param {String} userId -                 "full_content": "# Contextual Understanding\n\nThis module provides contextual understanding capabilities for the Open-Source Chatbots Platform, enabling chatbots to maintain conversation state and resolve references across multiple messages.\n\n## Features\n\n- **Conversation Context Management**: Maintains state across multiple conversation turns\n- **Entity Tracking**: Tracks entities mentioned throughout a conversation\n- **Reference Resolution**: Resolves pronouns and references to previously mentioned entities\n- **Intent Memory**: Remembers previous intents to understand follow-up questions\n- **Conversation History**: Stores and retrieves conversation history\n\n## Core Concepts\n\n### Conversation Context\n\nA conversation context represents a single conversation session and contains:\n\n- **Entities**: Entities mentioned during the conversation\n- **Intents**: Intents detected throughout the conversation\n- **References**: References to previously mentioned entities\n- **Messages**: The history of messages in the conversation\n- **Metadata**: Additional information about the conversation\n\n### Reference Resolution\n\nThe module can resolve references in messages, such as:\n\n- **Pronouns**: \"he\", \"she\", \"it\", \"they\", etc.\n- **Demonstratives**: \"this\", \"that\", \"these\", \"those\"\n- **Implicit References**: References to previously mentioned entities without explicitly naming them\n\n## Usage\n\n### Basic Usage\n\n```javascript\nconst { nlpService } = require('./nlp/nlp.service');\n\n// Create a conversation context\nconst userId = 'user123';\nconst context = await nlpService.createConversationContext(userId, {\n  channel: 'web',\n  locale: 'en-US'\n});\n\n// Process a message with context\nconst result = await nlpService.processTextWithContext(\n  \"What's the weather like in New York?\",\n  context.id,\n  ['entities', 'intent']\n);\n\n// Process a follow-up message with reference resolution\nconst followUpResult = await nlpService.processTextWithContext(\n  \"What about tomorrow?\",\n  context.id,\n  ['entities', 'intent']\n);\n\n// The system will understand that \"tomorrow\" refers to the weather in New York\nconsole.log(followUpResult.context.resolvedReferences);\n```\n\n### Accessing Conversation History\n\n```javascript\n// Get conversation history\nconst history = await nlpService.getConversationHistory(context.id, 10);\n\n// Display conversation\nhistory.forEach(message => {\n  console.log(`${message.role}: ${message.text}`);\n});\n```\n\n### Accessing Active Entities\n\n```javascript\n// Get the current context\nconst context = await nlpService.getConversationContext(contextId);\n\n// Access entities by type\nconst locations = context.entities.LOC || [];\nconst people = context.entities.PERSON || [];\n\n// Use entities in response generation\nif (locations.length > 0) {\n  console.log(`I see you're interested in ${locations[0].value}`);\n}\n```\n\n## Integration with NLP Service\n\nThe contextual understanding module is fully integrated with the NLP service, allowing it to be used seamlessly with other NLP features:\n\n```javascript\n// Process text with multiple NLP features and context\nconst result = await nlpService.processTextWithContext(\n  text,\n  contextId,\n  ['entities', 'intent', 'sentiment'],\n  { userId }\n);\n\n// Access NLP results\nconst entities = result.entities;\nconst intent = result.intent;\nconst sentiment = result.sentiment;\n\n// Access context information\nconst resolvedReferences = result.context.resolvedReferences;\nconst activeEntities = result.context.activeEntities;\nconst recentIntents = result.context.recentIntents;\n```\n\n## Context Lifecycle\n\n1. **Creation**: A context is created at the start of a conversation\n2. **Updates**: The context is updated with each message\n3. **Expiration**: Contexts expire after a configurable period of inactivity (default: 30 minutes)\n4. **Cleanup**: Expired contexts are automatically cleaned up\n\n## Configuration\n\nThe context management service can be configured with the following options:\n\n```javascript\n// Environment variables\nprocess.env.CONTEXT_TTL_MINUTES = '60'; // Context time-to-live in minutes\nprocess.env.MAX_CONTEXTS_PER_USER = '10'; // Maximum contexts per user\n\n// Or through initialization options\nawait contextManagementService.initialize({\n  contextTTL: 60 * 60 * 1000, // 60 minutes in milliseconds\n  maxContextsPerUser: 10\n});\n```\n\n## Performance Considerations\n\n- Contexts are stored in memory for fast access and periodically persisted to storage\n- Expired contexts are automatically cleaned up to prevent memory leaks\n- The number of contexts per user is limited to prevent resource exhaustion\n\n## Requirements\n\n- Node.js 14+\n- Local storage service (for persistence)\n\n## License\n\nThis component is licensed under the MIT License, the same as the main project.\n",

These integrations allow the chatbot platform to perform natural language processing tasks locally without relying on external API services.\n\n## Available Engines\n\n### spaCy Engine\n\nThe spaCy engine provides integration with the [spaCy](https://spacy.io/) Python library, which offers industrial-strength natural language processing capabilities.\n\nFeatures:\n- Entity extraction\n- Part-of-speech tagging\n- Dependency parsing\n- Noun chunk extraction\n- Keyword extraction\n- Basic sentiment analysis\n\n### NLTK Engine\n\nThe NLTK engine provides integration with the [Natural Language Toolkit (NLTK)](https://www.nltk.org/), a leading platform for building Python programs to work with human language data.\n\nFeatures:\n- Entity extraction\n- Keyword extraction\n- Sentiment analysis using VADER\n- Part-of-speech tagging\n- Tokenization\n\n## Setup Requirements\n\nTo use these engines, you need to have Python installed on your system along with the required libraries:\n\n### For spaCy:\n```bash\npip install spacy\npython -m spacy download en_core_web_md  # Download English model\n```\n\n### For NLTK:\n```bash\npip install nltk\npython -c \"import nltk; });\n      \n      pythonProcess.on('close', (code) => {\n        if (code === 0) {\n          try {\n            const parsedResult = JSON.parse(result);\n            resolve(parsedResult);\n                 "full_content": "# Advanced Intent Classification\n\nThis module provides advanced intent classification capabilities for the Open-Source Chatbots Platform using local models that can run directly in Node.js without requiring external services.\n\n## Features\n\n- **Local Processing**: Uses TensorFlow.js for local model inference\n- **Rule-Based Fallback**: Provides a rule-based fallback mechanism when TensorFlow.js is not available\n- **Domain-Specific Intents**: Supports domain-specific intent classification\n- **Confidence Scoring**: Provides confidence scores for classified intents\n- **Custom Intents**: Allows adding custom intents with examples\n- **Persistence**: Saves intent examples to local storage for reuse\n\n## Models\n\nThe intent classification service supports the following models:\n\n1. **Universal Sentence Encoder (TensorFlow.js)**:\n   - A lightweight model that converts text into embeddings for semantic similarity\n   - Can be loaded directly from TensorFlow Hub or saved locally\n\n2. **Rule-Based Classification**:\n   - Uses Jaccard similarity for text matching\n   - Provides a fallback when TensorFlow.js is not available\n\n## Usage\n\n### Basic Usage\n\n```javascript\nconst { intentClassificationService } = require('./nlp/intent');\n\n// Initialize the service\nawait intentClassificationService.initialize();\n\n// Classify intent from text\nconst text = \"What's the weather like in New York today?\";\nconst result = await intentClassificationService.classifyIntent(text);\n\nconsole.log(result);\n// Output:\n// {\n//   intent: \"weather\",\n//   confidence: 0.85,\n//   intents: [\n//     { intent: \"weather\", confidence: 0.85 },\n//     { intent: \"location\", confidence: 0.42 }\n//   ]\n// }\n```\n\n### Adding Custom Intents\n\n```javascript\n// Add a custom intent with examples\nawait intentClassificationService.addIntent(\n  'weather',\n  [\n    \"What's the weather like today?\",\n    \"Will it rain tomorrow?\",\n    \"What's the temperature outside?\",\n    \"Is it going to snow this weekend?\",\n    \"How's the weather in London right now?\"\n  ]\n);\n\n// Classify intent\nconst text = \"Is it going to be sunny tomorrow?\";\nconst result = await intentClassificationService.classifyIntent(text);\n\n// Output will include the custom intent if it matches\n```\n\n### Domain-Specific Intents\n\n```javascript\n// Add domain-specific intents\nawait intentClassificationService.addIntent(\n  'symptom_check',\n  [\n    \"I have a headache\",\n    \"My throat hurts\",\n    \"I'm feeling dizzy\",\n    \"I have a fever\"\n  ],\n  'healthcare' // Domain ID\n);\n\n// Classify intent with domain-specific context\nconst text = \"I've been having a persistent cough\";\nconst result = await intentClassificationService.classifyIntent(text, {\n  domainId: 'healthcare'\n});\n\n// Output will include domain-specific intents\n```\n\n## Configuration\n\nThe intent classification service can be configured with the following options:\n\n```javascript\nawait intentClassificationService.initialize({\n  defaultModel: 'universal-sentence-encoder', // Default model to use\n  fallbackToRules: true, // Fall back to rule-based classification if TensorFlow.js is not available\n  confidenceThreshold: 0.7, // Minimum confidence score for intents\n  enabledModels: ['universal-sentence-encoder', 'rules'] // Models to enable\n});\n```\n\n## Integration with NLP Service\n\nThe intent classification service is integrated with the main NLP service, allowing it to be used seamlessly with other NLP features:\n\n```javascript\nconst nlpService = require('../nlp.service');\n\n// Process text with multiple NLP features\nconst result = await nlpService.processText(text, ['intent', 'entities', 'sentiment']);\n\n// Access intent from the result\nconst intent = result.intent;\n```\n\n## Requirements\n\n- Node.js 14+ with the following packages:\n  - @tensorflow/tfjs-node (optional, for TensorFlow.js support)\n  - uuid\n\n## Performance Considerations\n\n- TensorFlow.js requires more memory and processing power than rule-based classification\n- For resource-constrained environments, enable the rule-based fallback\n- The first run of TensorFlow.js will be slower due to model loading\n- Pre-computing embeddings for intent examples improves classification speed\n\n## License\n\nThis component is licensed under the MIT License, the same as the main project.\n",

            "full_content": "# Local Storage Implementation\n\nThis directory contains the local storage implementation for the Open-Source Chatbots Platform. The local storage service provides a way to store and retrieve chatbot data locally without relying on external services.\n\n## Features\n\n- **Multiple Storage Backends**: Supports both file-based and SQLite storage options\n- **Document-Oriented API**: Simple API for storing, retrieving, querying, and deleting data\n- **Collection-Based Organization**: Data is organized into collections (users, bots, conversations, etc.)\n- **Query Capabilities**: Supports filtering, sorting, pagination, and advanced query operators\n- **Automatic ID Generation**: Automatically generates UUIDs for new items if not provided\n- **Timestamp Management**: Automatically adds and updates timestamps for created and modified items\n\n## Configuration\n\nThe local storage service can be configured using environment variables:\n\n- `LOCAL_STORAGE_TYPE`: Storage backend type ('file' or 'sqlite', default: 'file')\n- `LOCAL_STORAGE_PATH`: Base path for file storage (default: './data')\n- `SQLITE_DB_PATH`: Path to SQLite database file (default: './data/chatbot.db')\n\nExample in `.env` file:\n```\nLOCAL_STORAGE_TYPE=sqlite\nLOCAL_STORAGE_PATH=./data\nSQLITE_DB_PATH=./data/chatbot.db\n```\n\n## Usage\n\n### Basic Usage\n\n```javascript\nconst { localStorageService } = require('./storage');\n\n// Initialize the storage service\nawait localStorageService.initialize();\n\n// Store data\nconst user = await localStorageService.store('users', 'user123', {\n  name: 'John Doe',\n  email: 'john@example.com'\n});\n\n// Retrieve data\nconst retrievedUser = await localStorageService.retrieve('users', 'user123');\n\n// Query data\nconst users = await localStorageService.query('users', { name: 'John Doe' });\n\n// Delete data\nawait localStorageService.delete('users', 'user123');\n```\n\n### Advanced Queries\n\n```javascript\n// Query with operators\nconst recentConversations = await localStorageService.query('conversations', {\n  created_at: { $gt: Date.now() - 86400000 } // Conversations from the last 24 hours\n});\n\n// Sorting and pagination\nconst sortedMessages = await localStorageService.query('messages', \n  { conversation_id: 'conv123' },\n  { sort: { created_at: 1 }, limit: 10, offset: 20 }\n);\n```\n\n## Collections\n\nThe local storage service supports the following collections:\n\n- **users**: User profiles and preferences\n- **bots**: Chatbot configurations and settings\n- **conversations**: Conversation metadata and state\n- **messages**: Individual messages within conversations\n- **settings**: Application settings and configurations\n\n## Storage Structure\n\n### File Storage\n\nWhen using file-based storage, data is organized as follows:\n\n```\ndata/\n  ├── users/\n  │   ├── user123.json\n  │   └── ...\n  ├── bots/\n  │   ├── bot123.json\n  │   └── ...\n  ├── conversations/\n  │   ├── conv123.json\n  │   └── ...\n  ├── messages/\n  │   ├── msg123.json\n  │   └── ...\n  └── settings/\n      ├── setting123.json\n      └── ...\n```\n\n### SQLite Storage\n\nWhen using SQLite storage, data is stored in tables with the following schema:\n\n- **users**: id, name, email, created_at, updated_at, data\n- **bots**: id, name, description, created_at, updated_at, data\n- **conversations**: id, user_id, bot_id, title, created_at, updated_at, data\n- **messages**: id, conversation_id, user_id, bot_id, content, type, created_at, data\n- **settings**: id, key, value, updated_at\n\n## Performance Considerations\n\n- **File Storage**: Better for small to medium datasets and development environments\n- **SQLite Storage**: Better for larger datasets and production environments with query-heavy workloads\n\n## Error Handling\n\nThe local storage service includes robust error handling and logging. All errors are logged with appropriate context to help with debugging.\n\n## Dependencies\n\n- **fs.promises**: For file system operations\n- **path**: For path manipulation\n- **sqlite3** and **sqlite**: For SQLite database operations\n- **uuid**: For generating unique identifiers\n- **logger**: For logging errors and information\n\n## Extending\n\nTo add a new storage backend:\n\n1. Add a new storage type option (e.g., 'mongodb')\n2. Implement initialization, store, retrieve, query, and delete methods for the new backend\n3. Update the constructor to handle the new storage type\n\n## License\n\nThis component is licensed under the MIT License, the same as the main project.\n",

The template system provides pre-defined configurations for common chatbot use cases, allowing users to quickly create and customize chatbots without starting from scratch.\n\n## Features\n\n- **Pre-defined Templates**: Ready-to-use templates for common chatbot use cases (customer support, sales, FAQ, education, personal assistant)\n- **Customization Options**: Ability to override any routes for template management\n\n## Default Templates\n\nThe system comes with several pre-defined templates:\n\n1. **Customer Support**: Template for customer support chatbots with responses for handling product inquiries, order status, returns, and complaints\n2. **Sales Assistant**: Template for sales and lead generation chatbots with responses for product inquiries, pricing, features, and purchase assistance\n3. **FAQ Bot**: Template for frequently asked questions chatbots with integration to knowledge bases\n4. **Educational Assistant**: Template for educational and tutoring chatbots with concept explanations, practice problems, and study tips\n5. **Personal Assistant**: Template for personal assistant chatbots with reminders, scheduling, weather, and note-taking persuasive, etc.\n    },\n    intents: [\n      'greeting',\n      'farewell',\n      // Other intents\n    ],\n    responses: {\n      greeting: 'Hello! I\\'m {{bot_name}}, your assistant. How can I help you today?',\n      farewell: 'Thank you for chatting with me. Have a great day!',\n      // Other responses\n    },\n    plugins: [\n      'plugin-id-1',\n      'plugin-id-2',\n      // Other plugins\n    ],\n    settings: {\n      // Template-specific settings\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n## API Endpoints\n\nThe template system exposes the following API endpoints:\n\n- `GET /api/templates`: Get all templates with optional filtering and pagination\n- `GET /api/templates/:id`: Get a specific template by ID\n- `POST /api/templates`: Create a new template (requires authentication)\n- `PUT /api/templates/:id`: Update an existing template (requires authentication)\n- `DELETE /api/templates/:id`: Delete a template (requires authentication)\n- `POST /api/templates/:templateId/apply/:botId`: Apply a template to an existing bot (requires authentication)\n- `POST /api/templates/:templateId/create-bot`: Create a new bot from a template (requires authentication)\n\n## Usage Examples\n\n### Creating a Bot from a Template\n\n```javascript\nconst { templateService } = require('./templates');\n\nasync function createCustomerSupportBot() {\n  const bot = await templateService.createBotFromTemplate(\n    'customer-support',\n    {\n      name: 'My Support Bot',\n      description: 'A customer support bot for my company'\n    },\n    {\n      // Customizations\n      responses: {\n        greeting: 'Hello! Define the template structure with appropriate personality, intents, responses, plugins, and settings\n2. Use the template service to create the template\n3. The template will be automatically available through the API\n\n## License\n\nThis component is licensed under the MIT License, the same as the main project.\n",

training domains (e.g., customer support, e-commerce, healthcare)\n- **Dataset Management**: Create, update, and manage training datasets for different domains\n- **Multiple Framework Support**: Integration with popular open-source training frameworks (Rasa, DeepPavlov, Botpress)\n- **File Management**: Upload, download, and manage training data files\n- **Training Jobs**: Start, monitor, and manage training jobs for chatbots\n- **Sample Data**: Pre-defined sample training data for common domains\n\n## Components\n\n- **Training Service**: Core service for managing domains, datasets, and library built on TensorFlow\n3. **Botpress**: Open-source conversational assistant creation platform\n\n## Domain Structure\n\nEach training domain has the following structure:\n\n```javascript\n{\n  id: 'domain-id',\n  name: 'Domain Name',\n  description: 'Domain description',\n  language: 'en', // ISO language code\n  created_at: 1621234567890,\n  updated_at: 1621234567890\n}\n```\n\n## Dataset 'Dataset Name',\n  description: 'Dataset description',\n  files: ['file1.yml', 'file2.yml'], // List of files in the dataset\n  created_at: 1621234567890,\n  updated_at: 1621234567890\n}\n```\n\n## Training Job Structure\n\nEach training job has the following structure:\n\n```javascript\n{\n  id: 'job-id',\n  bot_id: 'bot-id',\n  dataset_id: 'dataset-id',\n  domain_id: 'domain-id',\n  framework: 'rasa',\n  status: 'pending', // pending, running, completed, failed\n  created_at: 1621234567890,\n  updated_at: 1621234567890,\n  completed_at: 1621234567890 // Only present if status is completed or failed\n}\n```\n\n## API Endpoints\n\nThe training system exposes the following API endpoints:\n\n### Domains\n\n- `GET /api/training/domains`: Get all training domains\n- `GET /api/training/domains/:id`: Get a specific domain by ID\n- `POST /api/training/domains`: Create a new domain\n- `PUT /api/training/domains/:id`: Update an existing domain\n- `DELETE /api/training/domains/:id`: Delete a domain\n\n### Datasets\n\n- `GET /api/training/datasets`: Get all training datasets\n- `GET /api/training/datasets/:id`: Get a specific dataset by ID\n- `POST /api/training/datasets`: Create a new dataset\n- `PUT /api/training/datasets/:id`: Update an existing dataset\n- `DELETE /api/training/datasets/:id`: Delete a dataset\n- `GET /api/training/datasets/:id/files/:fileName`: Get a specific file from a dataset\n\n### Training\n\n- `POST /api/training/bots/:botId/train/:datasetId`: Train a bot using a specific dataset\n- `GET /api/training/jobs`: Get all training jobs\n- `GET /api/training/jobs/:id`: Get a specific training job by ID\n- `GET /api/training/frameworks`: Get available training frameworks\n\n## Usage training is completed\n- **NLP Service**: Trained models can be used by the NLP service for intent recognition and entity extraction\n\n## Sample Data\n\nThe system comes with sample training data for
